texts.preamble: M/S Sabu Trade Pvt Ltd vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 17 November, 2016 Author: P.N.Prakash Bench: P.N.Prakash In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated: 17.11.2016 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice P.N.Prakash Crl.OP No.24678 of 2016 and Crl.M.P.No.11866 of 2016 1.M/s Sabu Trade Pvt Ltd rep by its Director G.Vikash Sabu 2.S.Gopal Sabu 3.G.Kaushalya Sabu 4.G.Vishal Sabu ..Petitioners Vs 1.The State of Tamil Nadu rep by its Secretary Department of Health and Family Welfare Secretariat, Chennai. 2.The Commissioner of Food Safety Office of the Commissioner of Food Safety 5th Floor, Dms Building Teynampet, Chennai 6. 3.The Designated Officer District Food Safety Office Salem 636 001. 4.The Food Safety Officer Soormangalam Zone-1 Salem District 636 001. 5.The Managing Director Sago Serve Jagirammpalayam, Omalur Main Road Salem 636 302. .. Respondents Prayer:- Criminal Original Petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., to call for the rec For Petitioners : Mr.C.Kanagaraj For Respondents : Mr.C.Emalias, M/S Sabu Trade Pvt Ltd vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 17 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107701660/ 1 Addl.Public Prosecutor O R D E R
texts.facts: This petition has been filed to call for the records and to quash the complaint in STC No.201 of 2016 dated 24.11.2015 pending on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No.III, Salem. 3. It is the case of the complainant that the accused are running a Company in the name M/s Sabu Trade Pvt Ltd., and are into wholesale and retail business in sago. The complainant visited the premises of the accused on 20.09.2013 and purchased 4 boxes of Sachamoti Agmark Tapioca Sago for Rs.150/-. He sent one packet of this sago to Food Analaysis Laboratory, Salem for analysis and report. The accused did not elect to send one sample to National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratory, though they have the right under the Food Safety Act. The report dated 30.09.2013 from the Food Analysis Laboratory, Salem is as follows: "Opinion: I am of the opinion that the sample of "Sago" specified under Regulation 2.4.14:2 is found to be "Unsafe" as per Section 3(1) of (zz)(i), (iii),(v) & (xi) and Sec.26, Sub-Sec.(1)&(2)(i)(ii)&(v) and Section 27(1) of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. Since it contains Optical Whitener (Stilbene derivative) a harmful ingredient." 4. A copy of the report was furnished to the accused by the complainant. The accused elected to send one sample to the Referral Food Laboratory, Kolkata and accordingly, one sample was sent there for analysis. The Analysis Report dated 31.12.2013 issued by the Referral Laboratory, Kolkata confirmed the findings of the Food Analysis Laboratory, Salem. Thereafter, the prosecution in this case was filed on 27.01.2016 before the Judicial Magistrate No.III, Salem and the same was taken on file on 10.06.2016 in STC No.201 of 2016, challenging which the accused are before this Court.
texts.arguments: 5. Mr.C.Kanagaraj, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the accused had purchased the sago in wholesale from "The Salem Sago Serve Co-operative Society" and therefore, they are not liable for any adulteration in that. 6. Per contra, Mr.C.Emalias, learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that this is a disputed question of fact, which cannot be gone into in a quash petition and that apart, the sago that was purchased by the Food Inspector bears the label of the accused Company. It is also possible for the accused to have adulterated it after having purchased in wholesale from "The Salem Sago Serve Co-operative Society". 7. There is much force in the submission of the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, as disputed questions of fact cannot be gone into in a prosecution u/s 482 Cr.P.C. M/S Sabu Trade Pvt Ltd vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 17 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107701660/ 2 8. The learned counsel for the petitioners pointed out certain infirmities in the two reports issued by the laboratories. I am afraid the infirmities in the report of an expert cannot be tested in a quash application and only when the witness is in the box, he can be asked to explain the infirmities, if any. 9. Lastly, the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the complaint should have been filed within one year from the date of lifting of sample, i.e. on or before 20.09.2014, whereas the complaint has been filed only on 27.01.2016. 10. Repelling this submission, learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that u/s 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Commissioner of Food Safety has been empowered to record his reasons in writing and approve the prosecution within an extended period of three years.
